items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

ctx.x: In Chicago? Yes. Yes. Every night I would stay up late and when my mother told me to go to bed, I'd

turn on the radio -- they would broadcast from the Three Deuces, and I used to hear Jimmy Noone, I used to hear Tatum, I used to hear Roy Eldridge. And, I used to catch Fletcher Henderson's band from The Grand Terrace -- it was on 40th and South part of Grand then, listening to "Christopher Columbus", that was his theme song.

Naturally, Earl Hines -- that was his home base, you might say. And let me see, that goes to '36, '35, and then when Basie came through -- I'd catch all those broadcasts. And they had little taverns in the neighborhood and they'd have 2 and 3 piece bands in there, and somebody would have a piano -- just everybody seemed to be in to music.
